statement: Given a joint distribution over random variables (X, Y) (or more generally X_1,...,X_n), the marginal distribution of a subset (e.g. X) is obtained by summing or integrating the joint distribution over the discarded variables (e.g. Y): discrete case p_X(x_i) = Σ_j p(x_i, y_j); continuous case f_X(x) = ∫ f(x,y) dy. The discarded variables (here Y) are said to be 'marginalized out'. [wikipedia:Marginal_distribution]

symbols.meaning: random variables with a known joint distribution
joint probability mass function of X and Y
joint probability density function of X and Y
collection of random variables in the multivariate case
symbols.dimensions: n scalars or vector of length n

properties.property: Discrete marginal pmf: p_X(x_i) = Σ_j p(x_i, y_j), and symmetrically p_Y(y_j) = Σ_i p(x_i, y_j).
properties.why: the marginal is found by summing the joint pmf over the values of the discarded variable

properties.property: Continuous marginal pdf: f_X(x) = ∫_c^d f(x,y) dy, and symmetrically f_Y(y) = ∫_a^b f(x,y) dx, for x∈[a,b], y∈[c,d].
properties.why: the marginal density is found by integrating the joint density over the discarded variable

properties.property: A marginal probability can be written as an expectation over the conditional: p_X(x) = ∫_y p_{X|Y}(x|y) p_Y(y) dy = E_Y[p_{X|Y}(x|Y)].
properties.why: averaging the conditional distribution of X given Y over the distribution of Y reproduces the marginal, by the law of the unconscious statistician

properties.property: Marginal cumulative distribution: F_X(x) = F(x,d) (or lim_{y→∞} F(x,y) if d=∞); symmetrically F_Y(y) = F(b,y).
properties.why: evaluating the joint CDF at the upper bound of the discarded variable's range removes dependence on that variable

properties.property: For n jointly distributed variables X_1,...,X_n, the marginal of X_i is obtained by summing (discrete) or integrating (continuous) the joint pmf/pdf over every other variable: p_{X_i}(k) = Σ p(x_1,...,x_{i-1},k,x_{i+1},...,x_n); f_{X_i}(x_i) = ∫...∫ f(x_1,...,x_n) dx_1...dx_{i-1}dx_{i+1}...dx_n.
properties.why: the same sum/integrate-out operation generalizes componentwise to any number of variables

properties.property: Marginalization differs from conditioning: the conditional distribution is the joint distribution divided by the other variable's marginal, e.g. f_{Y|X}(y|x) = f_{X,Y}(x,y) / f_X(x), whereas the marginal makes no reference to the other variable's value at all.
properties.why: distinguishes the operation of discarding a variable (marginal) from the operation of fixing its value (conditional)

assumptions.assumption: The joint distribution (pmf, pdf, or CDF) of the full variable set is known or specified.
assumptions.breaks_when: only marginals or conditionals are known without enough structure to reconstruct the joint — marginals alone do not determine the joint distribution (correlation/dependence is lost).

assumptions.assumption: For the continuous case, the joint density f(x,y) exists and is integrable over the discarded variable's domain.
assumptions.breaks_when: the joint distribution has no density (e.g. purely singular or mixed discrete-continuous components) or the integral diverges.

assumptions.assumption: The discarded variable's domain is fixed/known ([c,d] for y in the density case, or all of its support in the discrete/multivariate sum).
assumptions.breaks_when: the support depends on the value of the retained variable in a way not accounted for in the limits of summation/integration.

failure_modes.mode: Treating the marginal as if it captured the full joint behavior
failure_modes.signature: using p_X(x) alone to reason about events that depend jointly on X and Y, producing wrong probabilities for joint events
failure_modes.cause: marginalization discards all information about dependence between X and the marginalized-out variable Y

failure_modes.mode: Incorrect marginal from mismatched summation/integration range
failure_modes.signature: computed marginal does not sum/integrate to 1
failure_modes.cause: summing or integrating over the wrong domain for the discarded variable, e.g. omitting part of its support

failure_modes.signature: reporting p_X(x) when the question asked for p(x|y) or vice versa
failure_modes.cause: marginal removes reference to the other variable entirely, while conditional fixes it at a particular value; the two source_id formulas differ by a division by p_X(x) or f_X(x)
